$comment: ACKNOWLEDGED findings for inert-valuesobject-keys.ts.
WHAT AN ENTRY IS. Not a suppression -- a dated, keyed, reasoned record that a `valuesObject` key
governs NOTHING and is not being repaired in the change that discovered it. Every acknowledged
finding is still printed by the report and still costs exactly what it costs; what the entry buys
is a non-red gate, never a working key.
WHY THESE ELEVEN ARE ACKNOWLEDGED RATHER THAN FIXED. Repairing them means editing manifests that
deploy to a live cluster -- a Service type, a replica topology, an attestor's verification mode.
Each is a change that deserves to be watched landing, and bundling eleven of them into the change
that introduces their detector would make the detector unreviewable and the repairs unwatched. The
guard's job is to make them impossible to lose; the repairs are the next change, not this one.
KEYED BY IDENTITY, NEVER BY LINE. `key` is `<appId> <valuesObject path>`. A manifest that grows a
line cannot silently re-arm or re-suppress a different defect.
`observed` PINS WHAT WAS ACKNOWLEDGED, byte for byte. If the chart is bumped and the key becomes
half-real, the text changes and the entry stops covering it. A baseline that keeps matching after
the thing it excused has moved is the vacuity class with a filename.
`liftsWhen` NAMES THE GATE THAT WOULD ACTUALLY CLEAR *THIS* ENTRY -- and that phrasing is the
repair of a trap found in this tree on 2026-08-22: a `LIFTS WHEN` STRICTER THAN THE GATE IT NAMES
keeps a deferral alive after its defect is gone. "Lifts when every chart in the tree renders
offline" does not lift when THIS key is fixed, so the entry outlives its own subject and the
ratchet stops ratcheting. Every condition below names one manifest edit and nothing larger.
STALE ENTRIES FAIL. An entry matching nothing is a claim about the tree that stopped being true.
Because each `liftsWhen` above is exactly "this key is fixed", fixing the key makes the entry
stale and the gate goes red until the entry is deleted -- which is the ratchet working, not
failing.

findings.reason: MEASURED 2026-08-22 against argo-rollouts 2.39.5: the chart's key is `dashboard.service.type` (values.yaml:66-68). `dashboard.serviceType` is one word away from real and reaches nothing, so the dashboard Service silently takes the chart default. Not repaired in the change that added this guard: changing a Service type is a live-cluster change and belongs in a change that can watch it land.
findings.liftsWhen: LIFTS WHEN this Application sets `dashboard.service.type` instead of `dashboard.serviceType` -- at which point this finding disappears and this entry goes STALE, which is itself refused.
findings.observed: `dashboard.serviceType` is not a key argo-rollouts@2.39.5 has: the chart's own values, its subcharts' values, and every `.Values` reference in its templates name no path at or under it, and no node containing it is consumed wholesale. Helm discards it silently, so the value declared here governs NOTHING: dashboard.serviceType

findings.reason: MEASURED 2026-08-22 against argo-rollouts 2.39.5: `notifications` has no `enabled` key. The chart gates notifications on `notifications.configmap.create` and `notifications.secret.create` (values.yaml:461+), both of which have their own defaults, so this line has never turned anything on or off.
findings.liftsWhen: LIFTS WHEN this Application drops `notifications.enabled` or replaces it with the `notifications.configmap.create` / `notifications.secret.create` pair the chart reads.
findings.observed: `notifications.enabled` is not a key argo-rollouts@2.39.5 has: the chart's own values, its subcharts' values, and every `.Values` reference in its templates name no path at or under it, and no node containing it is consumed wholesale. Helm discards it silently, so the value declared here governs NOTHING: notifications.enabled

findings.reason: MEASURED 2026-08-22 against dapr 1.14.4: `charts/dapr_placement` has no `replicaCount`. Its StatefulSet hardcodes `replicas: 0 / 3 / 1` chosen by `.Values.ha` and `.Values.scaleZero` (dapr_placement_statefulset.yaml:14-18), so the placement service's replica count has never come from this line. The value it names happens to equal what `ha: false` already produces, which is exactly why nobody noticed.
findings.liftsWhen: LIFTS WHEN this Application stops declaring `dapr_placement.replicaCount` -- either dropped, or the intended placement topology expressed through `dapr_placement.ha` (and `scaleZero`), which is what the chart reads.
findings.observed: `dapr_placement.replicaCount` is not a key dapr@1.14.4 has: the chart's own values, its subcharts' values, and every `.Values` reference in its templates name no path at or under it, and no node containing it is consumed wholesale. Helm discards it silently, so the value declared here governs NOTHING: dapr_placement.replicaCount

findings.reason: MEASURED 2026-08-22 against headlamp 0.30.1: the string `watchNamespaces` does not occur anywhere in the chart -- not in values.yaml, not in any template. headlamp's `config` block carries `inCluster`, `baseURL`, `pluginsDir`, `extraArgs` and `oidc`, and namespace scoping is not among them. So the Application declares a namespace restriction that has never been applied.
findings.liftsWhen: LIFTS WHEN this Application stops declaring `config.watchNamespaces` -- either dropped, or expressed through a mechanism headlamp 0.30.1 actually reads.
findings.observed: `config.watchNamespaces` is not a key headlamp@0.30.1 has: the chart's own values, its subcharts' values, and every `.Values` reference in its templates name no path at or under it, and no node containing it is consumed wholesale. Helm discards it silently, so the value declared here governs NOTHING: config.watchNamespaces

findings.reason: MEASURED 2026-08-22 against spire 0.24.2, and CONFIRMED BY THE CHART'S OWN README (line 124): "In previous versions, the setting spire-agent.workloadAttestors.k8s.skipKubeletVerification was set to true by default. Starting in 0.23.x, we removed that setting and replaced it with" `workloadAttestors.k8s.verification.type`. The pin is 0.24.2, so this key was removed two minor versions before the pin and the manifest still sets it. This is the highest-consequence entry in this file: it governs whether the agent verifies the kubelet, and it governs nothing.
findings.liftsWhen: LIFTS WHEN this Application stops declaring `spire-agent.workloadAttestors.k8s.skipKubeletVerification` -- the key spire removed in 0.23.x -- and expresses the intent through `spire-agent.workloadAttestors.k8s.verification` (whose `type` defaults to `skip` in 0.24.2) instead.
findings.observed: `spire-agent.workloadAttestors.k8s.skipKubeletVerification` is not a key spire@0.24.2 has: the chart's own values, its subcharts' values, and every `.Values` reference in its templates name no path at or under it, and no node containing it is consumed wholesale. Helm discards it silently, so the value declared here governs NOTHING: spire-agent.workloadAttestors.k8s.skipKubeletVerification

findings.reason: MEASURED 2026-08-22 against weaviate 17.6.0: the ollama modules accept ONLY `enabled` in this chart version. `templates/_helpers.tpl:50,134` reads `(index .Values "modules" "<module>" "enabled")` and nothing else, and values.yaml:1183,1692 declare the two blocks with `enabled` as their sole key -- unlike the sibling octoai modules, which do carry an `apiKey`. So the endpoint and model this cluster believes it has configured for Ollama are not reaching the pod from here; they would have to come from the container's environment. Four entries rather than one because each is a separate declared value that governs nothing.
findings.liftsWhen: LIFTS WHEN this Application stops declaring `modules.generative-ollama.apiEndpoint` -- either dropped, or moved to whatever weaviate 17.6.0 does read for the Ollama endpoint/model (its environment), or the pin moves to a chart version whose ollama module block carries this key.
